title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 39
paragraphs: The young man answered: “Father, it is understandable that you should take care of me after having seen such a vision. But there is a point you do not grasp, and in which the meaning of the dream has escaped you, and it is right that I should explain it to you. You say the dream declared that I would end my life by an iron spear-point. But what hands has a boar, or what iron spear-point, of which you are afraid? If the dream had told you that I would end my life by a tusk, or by some other thing resembling one, then it would indeed be right for you to do as you are doing. But it said ‘by a spear-point.’ Since, therefore, our fight will not be with men, let me now go.”
